S1_incident_reporting.rule_summary: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their unit or model, and provide immediate safety instructions.
S1_incident_reporting.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must report any thermal incident involving fire, smoke, uncontrolled overheating, injury, or property damage to the relevant regulator within 24 hours of learning of it, with a written incident report within 10 days. They must notify affected customers within 72 hours when an incident indicates a credible safety risk to their unit or model, and provide immediate safety instructions. Reports must include known incident counts, installed-unit denominators, and corrective actions; updates are required as material facts emerge.

parameters.quote: The 5% failure rate is a safety benchmark, not an automatic sales-eligibility limit. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to the regulator, and disclose the exact per-model results to current and prospective customers of that model. Exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit sales; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or sales restrictions based on evidence of risk.

S2_thermal_testing.rule_summary: The 5% failure rate is a safety benchmark, not an automatic sales-eligibility limit. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to the regulator, and disclose the exact per-model results to current and prospective customers of that model. Exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit sales; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or sales restrictions based on evidence of risk.
S2_thermal_testing.final_rule_text: Each model must undergo a documented sustained-heat test at 55 °C before sale and at least annually thereafter, using a regulator-approved protocol and representative production units. The 5% failure rate is a safety benchmark, not an automatic sales-eligibility limit. A model exceeding it must promptly undergo root-cause analysis, corrective action, and regulator-supervised retesting on a defined schedule. Manufacturers must submit complete per-model results, sample sizes, and corrective-action plans to the regulator, and disclose the exact per-model results to current and prospective customers of that model. Exceeding 5% alone does not prohibit sales; the regulator may impose proportionate interim safeguards or sales restrictions based on evidence of risk.

parameters.quote: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified annual rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units. Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices promptly when new information indicates a credible risk, including the affected model, risk, immediate precautions, and available remedies.

S5_customer_disclosure.rule_summary: A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified annual rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units. Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices promptly when new information indicates a credible risk, including the affected model, risk, immediate precautions, and available remedies.
S5_customer_disclosure.final_rule_text: Manufacturers must provide customers with clear safety notices promptly when new information indicates a credible risk, including the affected model, risk, immediate precautions, and available remedies. Incident rates must use a documented, consistently applied method and current installed-unit denominators, with supporting records available to the regulator. The regulator may promptly verify the calculation; verification must not delay interim protective measures or required customer safety notices. A manufacturer must initiate a recall when the verified annual rate for any model exceeds 8 thermal incidents per 100,000 installed units. The recall must provide affected customers with appropriate repair, replacement, or refund instructions and must be proportionate to the identified risk. A recall under this section does not by itself prohibit future sales of the model; any sales restriction requires a separate, evidence-based regulator determination. Manufacturers must notify affected customers and the regulator without delay, and report recall progress and incident-rate updates. Required notices and remedies must not be delayed while an investigation is ongoing.

judge_section_notes: S2 is the decisive Northwind win: the 5% figure is only a benchmark, so a model above it (Hearth 10 at 6.2%) can keep selling while corrective action proceeds, though exact per-model rates go to that model's customers. S5 mandates a recall above 8 per 100,000 with no interim period, which would reach Halcyon's Ember 8 at 9.9, while the recall does not itself bar future sales. S3 (six-year retrofit) and S4 (36-month suppression start) also favour the companies with the lower installed-base and suppression-cost exposure, respectively. The S3 adoption-relative deadline could not be converted to months because the adoption date is not stated.
